Without such an abstraction, conventional placement under the existing DRAM address mapping can subject structured tile accesses to severe row-buffer conflicts. We present TileDRAM, a compiler-runtime toolchain that introduces tile-to-DRAM layouts as a compiler-visible abstraction for DRAM placement. TileDRAM extends the GPU Linear Layout abstraction from compute-side mapping targets to DRAM placement coordinates and selects layouts per tile access signature, using recurring tile-local access behavior as the specialization unit. Since row-buffer locality depends on ordered request history, TileDRAM evaluates candidate layouts through their row-buffer behavior under fixed DRAM address mappings. Accesses under the selected layouts are realized through ordinary address arithmetic, without new address-remapping hardware or ISA support. In full-trace replay on Accel-Sim/Ramulator2 across 108 mixture-of-experts (MoE) feed-forward network (FFN) cases, TileDRAM reduces the request-weighted row-conflict rate from 75.7% to 15.2% and achieves a 1.77x geomean speedup. Retargeting six traces to six 3D DRAM organizations yields a 2.20x geomean speedup under the same compiler abstraction. On an RTX 3090, address transformation adds 0.17% geomean overhead over identity.

contribution.en: Introduces compiler-visible tile-to-DRAM layouts and selects them per tile access signature to reduce row-buffer conflicts in 3D DRAM GPGPUs.
contribution.zh: 引入编译器可见的tile到DRAM布局，并按tile访问特征选择布局以降低3D DRAM GPGPU行缓冲冲突。

why_care.en: Directly connects tiling and layout code generation with DRAM address mapping and GPU memory locality.
why_care.zh: 直接将tiling/布局代码生成与DRAM地址映射和GPU内存局部性联系起来。

recommendations.title: TileDRAM: Compiler-Controlled Tile-to-DRAM Layouts for 3D DRAM GPGPUs

recommendations.abstract: DRAM-based Processing-in-Memory (PIM) addresses the "memory wall" by executing computations directly inside main memory. However, memory interleaving and virtual memory limit contiguous data size visible to PIM units, constraining PIM task granularity. To mitigate this, existing PIM systems drastically isolate PIM memory or disable memory interleaving. These design choices, however, decrease the CPU memory bandwidth and introduce extra data transfer, leading to an additional "system memory wall" that must be resolved to realize PIM's full potential. In this work, we propose GUMPIM, a PIM system that allows interleaved CPU pages and non-interleaved PIM pages to coexist in a Unitary and Malleable memory space with Guaranteed PIM page allocation. GUMPIM enables zero-copy during PIM task offloading and maintains CPU memory bandwidth while ensuring low PIM offloading overhead. First, we propose a dual-track memory management mechanism consisting of independent page allocation and address translation for CPU and PIM pages. Second, we design GUMPIM interface hardware on PIM-enabled DRAMs to provide a dynamic address mapping for the different data layouts of CPU and PIM pages. Third, we propose a PIM-assisted page migration mechanism that transparently migrates pages while preserving CPU access bandwidth, thereby enabling guaranteed and accelerated PIM page allocation. GUMPIM requires no changes to commodity DRAM standards; all hardware modifications are limited to the DRAM side, ensuring full compatibility with existing CPUs and enabling immediate deployment on current HBMx- and LPDDRx-based PIM platforms. Our results show only <0.1% performance degradation for CPU workloads on GUMPIM. For PIM workloads, GUMPIM reduces memory allocation and CPU-part computation times by 2.7x and 4.93x, respectively, yielding an end-to-end 2.3x speedup over a state-of-the-art baseline system.
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong

contribution.en: Proposes a unitary PIM memory space with guaranteed PIM pages, dual-track translation, and migration to enable zero-copy offload without sacrificing CPU bandwidth.
contribution.zh: 提出统一PIM内存空间与保证PIM页、双轨地址转换和迁移机制，实现零拷贝卸载且不牺牲CPU带宽。

why_care.en: Informs PIM runtime and data-placement constraints that compiler-managed PIM offloading must respect.
why_care.zh: 揭示编译器管理PIM卸载时必须遵守的运行时与数据放置约束。

recommendations.title: GUMPIM: Unitary and Malleable Memory for Processing-in-Memory with Guaranteed PIM Pages

recommendations.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on edge devices enables personalized large language model (LLM) inference while preserving privacy. However, RAG's inherent length asymmetry makes the prefill phase the dominant bottleneck. While precomputing the KV caches offline alleviates the prefill cost on server systems, the multi-gigabyte caches over the narrow interconnect create a severe I/O wall for on-device systems. To mitigate this, we propose MemLLM, an end-to-end in-storage processing (ISP) architecture that executes the complete attention pipeline based on precomputed KV caches within the SSD. MemLLM utilizes per-channel accelerators to fully utilize the aggregated NAND channel bandwidth and accelerates all KV cache-related computations on the storage-side to minimize PCIe transfers. To efficiently handle the sparse updates required by RAG, MemLLM introduces a fused recomputation-query kernel paired with a hardware-based filter logic to halve the NAND read volume and eliminate write-back penalties. Furthermore, MemLLM's global SRAM-based stateful reduction engine enables a completely DRAM-less dataflow, thereby removing the internal memory bottlenecks and bounding the PCIe egress to an $O(1)$ footprint. A full-stack software stack allows asynchronous, zero-copy transfers from the ISP to the host and provides transparent execution within modern ML frameworks. Evaluated across eight real-world RAG datasets and six on-device LLM models, MemLLM achieves an average end-to-end speedup of 4.06$\times$ over the GPU baseline.

contribution.en: Designs an in-storage processor that runs full KV-cache-based attention inside the SSD to cut PCIe transfers for on-device RAG.
contribution.zh: 设计在SSD内执行完整KV缓存注意力流程的存内处理器，以减少端侧RAG的PCIe传输。

why_care.en: A near-memory and storage-acceleration point relevant to PIM dataflow and compiler-architecture co-design.
why_care.zh: 属于近内存/存储加速方向，与PIM数据流及编译架构协同设计相关。

recommendations.title: MemLLM: End-to-end In-Storage Acceleration of On-device Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Precomputed KV Caches
